children: Polish interest rates will likely remain stable for one or two quarters, central banker Ireneusz Dabrowski told state news agency PAP in comments published on Tuesday, adding that after the first quarter of 2027 a rate cut is more likely than a hike.

The National Bank of Poland kept its main interest rate at 3.75% last Wednesday, maintaining its cautious approach as rising commodity prices and increased energy costs create a risk of higher inflation.

"The most likely scenario for monetary policy is that interest rates will remain unchanged for one or two quarters; thereafter, after the first quarter of 2027, I see a greater likelihood of a rate cut than a rate rise," Dabrowski was quoted as saying by PAP.

"Over the next two quarters, I see a negligible risk of rate rises... In my view, stable rates until the end of the first quarter of 2027 is a scenario with a probability of around 90%. After that, decisions will depend on the data," he added.

Central banker Marcin Zarzecki told Reuters that Polish interest rates could remain unchanged until the end of this year, though a first-quarter 2027 hike cannot be ruled out if a commodities shock has a lasting impact on inflation.
